invariants_created: OPTIONS must be the first method sent in a session to discover server capabilities (observed in all 6 sessions as the initial request).
DESCRIBE must follow OPTIONS and precede SETUP in the standard lifecycle (OPTIONS → DESCRIBE → SETUP → PLAY → TEARDOWN).
SETUP must precede PLAY, PAUSE, and RECORD. No media delivery method can be issued before transport is established.
PLAY can only be issued after a successful SETUP (state READY). After PAUSE, PLAY resumes from READY state.
PAUSE can only be issued in PLAYING state (after PLAY). It transitions to READY state.
TEARDOWN terminates the session and transitions to INIT state. Session identifier becomes invalid after TEARDOWN.
OPTIONS can be sent at any point in the session lifecycle without affecting state.
GET_PARAMETER can be sent during PLAYING state as a keep-alive mechanism.
DESCRIBE may be retried on failure (e.g., 404 Not Found) before proceeding to SETUP.
The complete standard lifecycle is: OPTIONS → DESCRIBE → SETUP → PLAY → TEARDOWN. PAUSE is optional between PLAY and TEARDOWN.
ALL.CSeq: Mandatory in every RTSP request and response. Must be a monotonically increasing integer per connection. Each request-response pair shares the same CSeq value.

SETUP.Transport: Mandatory in SETUP request. Specifies transport mechanism: protocol profile (RTP/AVP), unicast/multicast, client_port range, delivery method (e.g., RTP/AVP;unicast;client_port=XXXX-XXXX). Server responds with confirmed transport parameters.
SETUP.Session: Returned by server in SETUP response. Becomes mandatory in all subsequent requests (PLAY, PAUSE, TEARDOWN, GET_PARAMETER, etc.) until session is terminated.
PLAY.Session: Mandatory. Must match the session identifier returned by the server in the SETUP response.
PAUSE.Session: Mandatory. Must match the session identifier returned by the server in the SETUP response.
TEARDOWN.Session: Mandatory. Must match the session identifier returned by the server in the SETUP response. After TEARDOWN, this session ID is no longer valid.
PLAY.Range: Optional but commonly used. Specifies NPT (Normal Play Time) or clock range for playback (e.g., 'npt=0.000-' for play from start).
DESCRIBE.Accept: Should be 'application/sdp' to indicate the client expects an SDP session description in the response.
DESCRIBE.Content-Type: In the response, must be 'application/sdp' when returning session description.
ANNOUNCE.Content-Type: Mandatory. Must be 'application/sdp' as the body contains an SDP session description.
OPTIONS.Public: Present in OPTIONS response only. Lists all methods supported by the server (e.g., 'Public: OPTIONS, DESCRIBE, SETUP, PLAY, PAUSE, TEARDOWN').
REDIRECT.Location: Mandatory in REDIRECT. Contains the new URI the client should redirect to.
GET_PARAMETER.Content-Length: May be 0 when used as a keep-alive ping with no body content.
RECORD.Session: Mandatory. Must match the session identifier returned by the server in the SETUP response.
RECORD.Range: Optional. Specifies NPT or clock range for recording duration.

status_changes.description: READY -> PLAYING via PLAY
status_changes.rationale: Directly observed in all 6 sessions with 200 OK response codes per trace evidence. Strong trace-level validation.

status_changes.description: PAUSED -> PLAYING via PLAY
status_changes.rationale: Conflicts with invariant evidence that PAUSE transitions to READY state (not PAUSED). Invariant claim 4 explicitly states 'After PAUSE, PLAY resumes from READY state.' The PAUSED state is not substantiated by doc evidence; the correct source state for PLAY after PAUSE is READY, which is already covered by claim 1.

status_changes.description: INIT -> INIT via OPTIONS
status_changes.rationale: Only supported by heuristic trace augmentation with no direct trace response-code evidence. Consistent with RTSP spec (OPTIONS is stateless) but lacks independent trace validation.

status_changes.description: INIT -> DESCRIBED via DESCRIBE
status_changes.rationale: Only supported by heuristic trace augmentation. No direct trace response-code evidence confirming this specific state transition. Consistent with spec but unvalidated by probe.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBED -> READY via SETUP
status_changes.rationale: Only supported by heuristic trace augmentation. No direct trace response-code evidence. Consistent with standard RTSP lifecycle but lacks independent trace confirmation.

status_changes.description: INIT -> READY via SETUP
status_changes.rationale: Only heuristic augmentation evidence. This transition bypasses DESCRIBE, which conflicts with the standard lifecycle invariant (OPTIONS→DESCRIBE→SETUP). While some RTSP implementations may allow it, there is no trace evidence of SETUP being issued without a preceding DESCRIBE.

status_changes.description: PLAYING -> PAUSED via PAUSE
status_changes.rationale: Conflicts with invariant evidence that PAUSE transitions from PLAYING to READY state, not to a PAUSED state. The doc-based invariant (claim 5) explicitly states 'PAUSE can only be issued in PLAYING state' and invariant 4 says it returns to READY. The PAUSED state is not validated by trace or doc evidence.

status_changes.description: PLAYING -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: Only heuristic augmentation evidence. Additionally conflicts with invariant 6 which claims TEARDOWN transitions to INIT (not CLOSED). The terminal state name is ambiguous — CLOSED vs INIT — and neither is directly validated by trace evidence observing post-TEARDOWN state.

status_changes.description: READY -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: Only heuristic augmentation evidence. Same CLOSED vs INIT ambiguity as claim 8. No trace evidence directly observing the post-TEARDOWN state.

status_changes.description: RECORDING -> CLOSED via TEARDOWN
status_changes.rationale: Only heuristic augmentation evidence with no trace observation of RECORDING state in any of the 6 sessions. The RECORDING state itself is unvalidated, making this transition speculative.

status_changes.description: OPTIONS must be the first method sent in a session to discover server capabilities (observed in all 6 sessions as the initial request).
status_changes.rationale: Directly observed in all 6 sessions: every session begins with OPTIONS -> 200. Strong trace-level evidence across the full session set.

status_changes.description: DESCRIBE must follow OPTIONS and precede SETUP in the standard lifecycle (OPTIONS → DESCRIBE → SETUP → PLAY → TEARDOWN).
status_changes.rationale: All 6 sessions follow OPTIONS then DESCRIBE then SETUP ordering per doc evidence. Directly observed sequencing across all sessions.

status_changes.description: SETUP must precede PLAY, PAUSE, and RECORD. No media delivery method can be issued before transport is established.
status_changes.rationale: SETUP -> 200 always precedes PLAY -> 200 in all sessions, directly validating the PLAY dependency. PAUSE dependency is indirectly supported (PAUSE follows PLAY which follows SETUP). RECORD dependency has no trace evidence.

status_changes.description: PLAY can only be issued after a successful SETUP (state READY). After PAUSE, PLAY resumes from READY state.
status_changes.rationale: Sessions 2 and 5 directly evidence SETUP -> PLAY -> PAUSE -> PLAY sequence with 200 OK responses, confirming both that PLAY requires prior SETUP and that PLAY resumes after PAUSE from READY state.

status_changes.description: PAUSE can only be issued in PLAYING state (after PLAY). It transitions to READY state.
status_changes.rationale: Sessions 2 and 5 show PLAY -> PAUSE -> 200, directly evidencing that PAUSE follows PLAY

ANNOUNCE.template:
ANNOUNCE rtsp://<host>:<port>/<path> RTSP/1.0
CSeq: <n>
Content-Type: application/sdp
Content-Length: <len>

<SDP body>

examples: integer, byte length of SDP body

DESCRIBE.template:
DESCRIBE rtsp://<host>:<port>/<path> RTSP/1.0
CSeq: <n>
Accept: application/sdp

examples: integer, byte length of SDP body in response

GET_PARAMETER.template:
GET_PARAMETER rtsp://<host>:<port>/<path> RTSP/1.0
CSeq: <n>
Session: <session-id>
Content-Length: <len>

examples: integer, byte length of body (may be 0 for keep-alive)
string, mandatory; session identifier from SETUP response

PLAY.template:
PLAY rtsp://<host>:<port>/<path> RTSP/1.0
CSeq: <n>
Session: <session-id>
Range: npt=<start>-<end>

examples: string, mandatory; session identifier from SETUP response

RECORD.template:
RECORD rtsp://<host>:<port>/<path> RTSP/1.0
CSeq: <n>
Session: <session-id>
Range: npt=<start>-<end>

examples: string, mandatory; session identifier from SETUP response
string, URI to redirect client to
string, session identifier returned by server in SETUP response; required in all subsequent requests

SET_PARAMETER.template:
SET_PARAMETER rtsp://<host>:<port>/<path> RTSP/1.0
CSeq: <n>
Session: <session-id>
Content-Type: <type>
Content-Length: <len>

<body>

examples: string, media type of parameter body
string, mandatory; session identifier from SETUP response
